title: Reporting cryptoasset user and transaction data
text:
If you provide cryptoasset services in the UK, you must collect data and report it to HMRC .

 This is because of rules called the Cryptoasset Reporting Framework ( CARF ).

 You can subscribe to get email updates about Cryptoasset Reporting Framework guidance.

 Information you need to report

 You need to collect details of all of your users , but you only need to report on users who are tax resident in the UK or another country that is signed up to CARF rules.

 You need to report these users’ details and a summary of their transactions.

 If you have no information to report in a year, you do not need to submit a report.

 How to create your report

 Your data must be submitted in XML file format.

 Each file can be up to 250MB — you can split your data into more than one file, if needed. It must not be a compressed zip file.

 To create your XML file, you must use the:

 • 
 XML schema on the Organisation for Economic Development ( OECD ) website — technical details that explain how your XML file must be structured and formatted

 • 

 HMRC file requirements and error messages ( ODS , 8.04 KB ) — rules that your data and the content of your file must follow

 How to submit your report

 You’ll need to upload your report to our online service. It’s not live yet — we’ll update the guidance when it is.

 When to report

 You need to submit your first report by 31 May 2027, giving details for 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026.

 In future years you’ll also need to submit a report by 31 May, giving details for the previous calendar year.

 Penalties

 If you do not follow the rules, we may charge you a penalty of up to £300 per user.

 You could be charged a penalty if:

 • you do not report

 • you submit your report late

 • if your report is inaccurate, incomplete or unverified

 Find out about penalties (International Exchange of Information Manual: IEIM8000600) .

 More information

 You can find detailed information about the Cryptoasset Reporting Framework:

 • in the International Exchange of Information technical manual 

 • in the rules and commentary on the OECD website 

 You can also find out about international tax transparency standards on the OECD ’s website .

 If you have questions about the Cryptoasset Reporting Framework, you can email  eoi.policy@hmrc.gov.uk .
changeNote: Added guidance about how to create your report, including a link to the 'HMRC file requirements and error messages' attachment. Removed the 1 January 2027 start date for submitting reports, as the online service will not be available from this date.
